ROM.1.1-3.text: Paul says he is set apart to preach God’s gospel

ROM.1.4-6.text: Paul was sent to call the Gentiles to obey by faith

ROM.1.7-7.text: Paul greets the believers in Rome with grace and peace

ROM.1.8-10.text: Paul thanks God for the Romans and prays to visit Rome

ROM.1.11-12.text: Paul wants to visit Rome to strengthen the believers

ROM.1.13-15.text: Paul often planned to visit Rome and preach the gospel

ROM.1.16-17.text: Paul is not ashamed of the gospel, God’s power to save

ROM.1.18-19.text: God’s anger is against people who hide the truth

ROM.1.20-21.text: People can see God in creation, yet do not thank him

ROM.1.22-23.text: People exchanged God’s glory for images

ROM.1.24-25.text: God gave people up to impurity because they chose lies

ROM.1.26-27.text: God gave people over to dishonorable passions

ROM.1.28-28.text: God gave people up to wrong thinking for rejecting him

ROM.1.29-31.text: People are filled with every kind of evil

ROM.1.32-32.text: People know sin deserves death yet approve it

ROM.2.1-2.text: Paul says those who judge others condemn themselves

ROM.2.3-4.text: God’s kindness leads people to turn from sin

ROM.2.5-7.text: God will repay each person for what he has done

ROM.2.8-9.text: God’s anger will come on all who do evil

ROM.2.10-12.text: God rewards all who do good and shows no favoritism

ROM.2.13-14.text: God accepts those who do the law, not only hear it

ROM.2.15-16.text: God will judge secret thoughts through Christ Jesus

ROM.2.17-20.text: Paul speaks to Jews who rely on the law and boast in God

ROM.2.21-22.text: Paul challenges Jews who teach others but break the law

ROM.2.23-24.text: Jews who break the law dishonor God among the Gentiles

ROM.2.25-27.text: Circumcision has value only if a person obeys the law

ROM.2.28-29.text: True Jews are Jews in heart, praised by God

ROM.3.1-2.text: Paul says Jews were trusted with God’s words

ROM.3.3-4.text: Human unfaithfulness does not cancel God’s faithfulness

ROM.3.5-6.text: Paul says God is not unjust to judge the world

ROM.3.7-8.text: Paul denies that people should do evil for good results

ROM.3.9-10.text: Paul says Jews and Greeks are all under sin

ROM.3.11-12.text: Scripture says no one seeks God or does good

ROM.3.13-14.text: Scripture says people’s words are deceitful and bitter

ROM.3.15-18.text: Paul says people are violent and do not fear God

ROM.3.19-20.text: The law shows that all people are guilty before God

ROM.3.21-22.text: God’s righteousness comes through faith to all who believe

ROM.3.23-24.text: All people have sinned, but God gives grace freely

ROM.3.25-26.text: God offered Jesus as a sacrifice to show he is just

ROM.3.27-28.text: Paul says faith, not works, leaves no room for boasting

ROM.3.29-30.text: God makes both Jews and Gentiles right by faith

ROM.3.31-31.text: Paul says faith does not cancel the law

ROM.4.1-3.text: Paul asks if Abraham was made right by works

check.why: Paul does not ask this question, and the draft ignores verse 3 where Abraham is made right by believing God.
check.suggestion: Abraham was made right because he believed God

ROM.4.4-5.text: God accepts the faith of those who do not work

ROM.4.6-8.text: David says people whose sins are forgiven are blessed

ROM.4.9-10.text: Abraham was made right before he was circumcised

ROM.4.11-12.text: Abraham is the father of all who believe

ROM.4.13-15.text: The promise to Abraham came by faith, not by law

ROM.4.16-17.text: The promise is for all who have Abraham’s faith

ROM.4.18-19.text: Abraham believed God’s promise although he was very old

ROM.4.20-22.text: Abraham trusted that God would do what he promised

ROM.4.23-25.text: Paul says the words about Abraham are also for believers

ROM.5.1-2.text: Believers have peace with God through Jesus

ROM.5.3-5.text: Believers rejoice in suffering and have hope

ROM.5.6-7.text: Christ died for the ungodly at the right time

ROM.5.8-9.text: God shows his love because Christ died for sinners

ROM.5.10-11.text: Believers are reconciled to God by the death of his Son

ROM.5.12-13.text: Sin and death came into the world through one man

ROM.5.14-15.text: Grace through Jesus Christ is greater than Adam’s sin

ROM.5.16-17.text: Believers will reign in life through Jesus Christ

ROM.5.18-19.text: One man’s sin brought condemnation; Christ brings life

ROM.5.20-21.text: Grace increases where sin increased and brings life

ROM.6.1-3.text: Paul says believers must not continue in sin

ROM.6.4-5.text: Believers walk in new life, united with Christ

ROM.6.6-7.text: Believers died with Christ and are free from sin

ROM.6.8-9.text: Believers who died with Christ will also live with him

ROM.6.10-11.text: Paul tells believers to count themselves dead to sin

ROM.6.12-14.text: Paul urges believers to offer themselves to God, not sin

ROM.6.15-16.text: Paul says believers must not sin because of grace

ROM.6.17-18.text: Paul thanks God that believers are free from sin

ROM.6.19-21.text: Paul urges believers to serve righteousness, not impurity

ROM.6.22-23.text: Sin pays with death, but God gives eternal life

ROM.7.1-1.text: Paul says the law rules a person only until death

ROM.7.2-3.text: A wife is free to marry again after her husband dies

ROM.7.4-5.text: Believers died to the law to belong to Christ

ROM.7.6-6.text: Believers are released from the law to serve in the Spirit

ROM.7.7-8.text: Paul says the law is not sin but shows what sin is

ROM.7.9-10.text: Paul says the commandment brought him death, not life

ROM.7.11-12.text: Sin deceived Paul, but the law is holy and good

ROM.7.13-14.text: Paul says sin used the good law to cause death

ROM.7.15-16.text: Paul does what he hates and not what he wants

ROM.7.17-18.text: Paul says sin that lives in him does the evil

ROM.7.19-21.text: Paul keeps doing the evil he does not want to do

ROM.7.22-23.text: Paul delights in God’s law, but sin holds him captive

ROM.7.24-25.text: Paul cries out for rescue and thanks God through Christ

ROM.8.1-2.text: Believers in Christ Jesus are no longer condemned

ROM.8.3-5.text: God sent his Son so believers can live by the Spirit

ROM.8.6-8.text: The mind of the flesh brings death; the Spirit brings life

ROM.8.9-10.text: The Spirit of Christ lives in believers

ROM.8.11-11.text: God will give life to believers’ bodies by his Spirit

ROM.8.12-13.text: Believers must not live by the flesh, but by the Spirit

ROM.8.14-15.text: Believers led by the Spirit are children of God

ROM.8.16-17.text: Believers are God’s children and heirs with Christ

ROM.8.18-19.text: Paul says present suffering is small beside future glory

ROM.8.20-22.text: Creation groans and waits to be set free

ROM.8.23-25.text: Believers wait patiently in hope for what is not yet seen

ROM.8.26-27.text: The Spirit helps believers who do not know how to pray

ROM.8.28-30.text: God works all things for the good of believers

ROM.8.31-32.text: God is for believers and gave his own Son

ROM.8.33-34.text: No one can condemn believers, because Christ intercedes

ROM.8.35-36.text: Paul asks what can separate believers from Christ’s love

ROM.8.37-39.text: Believers are more than conquerors through Christ

ROM.9.1-2.text: Paul tells the truth about his deep sorrow

ROM.9.3-5.text: Paul would accept a curse for his own people Israel

ROM.9.6-7.text: God’s word has not failed; only some are true Israel

ROM.9.8-9.text: God’s children are the children of the promise

ROM.9.10-13.text: God chose Jacob, not Esau, before the twins were born

ROM.9.14-16.text: God is not unjust; he gives mercy as he chooses

ROM.9.17-18.text: God shows mercy to whom he wants and hardens others

ROM.9.19-21.text: Paul answers: no one can talk back to God

ROM.9.22-24.text: God calls believers from both Jews and Gentiles

ROM.9.25-26.text: God will call those who are not his people his children

ROM.9.27-29.text: Isaiah says only a remnant of Israel will be saved

ROM.9.30-31.text: Gentiles received righteousness by faith, but Israel did not

ROM.9.32-33.text: Israel stumbled because it sought righteousness by works

ROM.10.1-3.text: Paul prays for the salvation of the Israelites

ROM.10.4-5.text: Christ brings righteousness to everyone who believes

ROM.10.6-7.text: Paul says no one must bring Christ down or up

check.why: The text does not forbid people from bringing Christ down or up, but says righteousness by faith does not ask who will do so.
check.suggestion: Faith does not ask who will bring Christ down or up

ROM.10.8-10.text: Whoever confesses Jesus as Lord and believes will be saved

ROM.10.11-13.text: The same Lord saves everyone who calls on him

ROM.10.14-15.text: People need preachers to hear and believe the good news

ROM.10.16-17.text: Not all welcomed the good news; faith comes by hearing

ROM.10.18-18.text: Paul says all people have heard the message

ROM.10.19-19.text: Moses said God will make Israel jealous of other nations

ROM.10.20-21.text: Isaiah says Israel is disobedient, but others found God

ROM.11.1-3.text: Paul says God has not rejected his people

ROM.11.4-5.text: God keeps a remnant chosen by grace

ROM.11.6-8.text: What Israel sought, only the chosen obtained

ROM.11.9-10.text: David says a trap and blindness will come on the hardened

ROM.11.11-12.text: Israel’s failure brings salvation to the Gentiles

ROM.11.13-14.text: Paul speaks to Gentiles about his hope to save some Jews

ROM.11.15-16.text: Israel’s acceptance will be life from the dead

ROM.11.17-18.text: Paul warns Gentile believers not to boast over branches

ROM.11.19-21.text: Paul warns Gentile believers not to be proud

ROM.11.22-22.text: Paul tells Gentile believers to continue in God’s kindness

ROM.11.23-24.text: God can graft Israel back in if Israel believes

ROM.11.25-25.text: Israel is hardened in part until all the Gentiles come in

ROM.11.26-27.text: All Israel will be saved when the Deliverer comes

ROM.11.28-29.text: God still loves Israel and his call does not change

ROM.11.30-32.text: God shows mercy to both Gentiles and Israel

ROM.11.33-34.text: Paul praises God’s deep wisdom and knowledge

ROM.11.35-36.text: Paul says all things come from God and are for his glory

ROM.12.1-2.text: Paul urges believers to be living sacrifices to God

ROM.12.3-3.text: Paul tells believers to think humbly and wisely

ROM.12.4-5.text: Believers are many members of one body in Christ

ROM.12.6-8.text: Paul tells believers to use the different gifts God gave

ROM.12.9-10.text: Paul urges believers to love sincerely and honor others

ROM.12.11-13.text: Believers should serve the Lord and help the needy

ROM.12.14-16.text: Believers should bless persecutors and live in harmony

ROM.12.17-18.text: Believers should not repay evil but live at peace

ROM.12.19-21.text: Believers must leave revenge to God and do good

ROM.13.1-2.text: Paul tells believers to submit to the authorities

ROM.13.3-5.text: Rulers are God’s servants, so believers should obey

ROM.13.6-7.text: Paul tells believers to pay taxes and give respect

ROM.13.11-12.text: Paul urges believers to wake up because salvation is near

ROM.13.13-14.text: Paul urges believers to live decently and follow Christ

ROM.14.1-2.text: Believers must accept those who are weak in faith

ROM.14.3-4.text: Believers must not judge each other about food

ROM.14.5-6.text: Believers may honor the Lord in different ways

ROM.14.7-9.text: Believers belong to the Lord in life and in death

ROM.14.10-11.text: All believers will stand before God’s judgment seat

ROM.14.12-12.text: Each believer will give an account to God

ROM.14.13-13.text: Paul tells believers not to cause others to stumble

ROM.14.14-15.text: Believers must not harm a brother by eating

ROM.14.16-17.text: God’s kingdom is peace and joy, not food and drink

ROM.14.18-19.text: Believers should serve Christ and pursue peace

ROM.14.20-21.text: Paul urges believers not to cause others to stumble

ROM.14.22-23.text: Paul says eating with doubt is sin

check.why: It only summarizes verse 23 and ignores the instruction about personal belief in verse 22.
check.suggestion: Paul says that whatever is not done from faith is sin

ROM.15.1-2.text: The strong should help the weak and please others

ROM.15.3-4.text: Christ did not please himself, and Scripture gives hope

ROM.15.5-6.text: Paul prays that believers will live in harmony

ROM.15.7-7.text: Believers should accept one another as Christ did

ROM.15.8-9.text: Christ served the Jews so that Gentiles would praise God

ROM.15.10-11.text: Scripture says the Gentiles will praise the Lord

ROM.15.12-12.text: Isaiah says the Gentiles will hope in the coming king

check.why: The text speaks of one who rules rather than a king.
check.suggestion: Isaiah says the Gentiles will hope in their ruler

ROM.15.13-13.text: Paul prays that God will fill believers with joy and peace

ROM.15.14-14.text: Paul is sure the believers are good and able to teach

ROM.15.15-16.text: Paul writes boldly as God’s minister to the Gentiles

ROM.15.17-19.text: Paul tells what Christ did through him among the Gentiles

ROM.15.20-21.text: Paul wants to preach where Christ is not known

ROM.15.22-22.text: Paul was often hindered from coming to the Romans

ROM.15.23-23.text: Paul has long wanted to visit the Romans

ROM.15.24-25.text: Paul plans to visit Rome on his way to Spain

check.why: It fits verse 24 but leaves out Paul’s journey to Jerusalem in verse 25.
check.suggestion: Paul plans to visit Rome after going to Jerusalem

ROM.15.26-27.text: Macedonia and Achaia gave money for the poor believers

ROM.15.28-29.text: Paul will go to Spain after he delivers the gift

ROM.15.30-32.text: Paul asks the believers to pray for his work in Jerusalem

ROM.15.33-33.text: Paul asks God to give peace to all the believers

check.why: Paul prays that the God of peace will be with them, not that God will give peace.
check.suggestion: Paul prays that the God of peace will be with them all

ROM.16.1-2.text: Paul asks the church to welcome and help Phoebe

ROM.16.3-5.text: Paul greets Prisca, Aquila, and Epenetus

ROM.16.6-8.text: Paul greets Mary, Andronicus, Junia, and Ampliatus

ROM.16.9-11.text: Paul greets Urbanus, Stachys, Apelles, and others

ROM.16.12-14.text: Paul greets Tryphena, Tryphosa, Persis, and others

ROM.16.15-16.text: Paul greets more believers and asks for a holy kiss

ROM.16.17-18.text: Paul warns believers to avoid people who cause divisions

ROM.16.19-20.text: Paul wants believers to be wise; God will crush Satan

ROM.16.21-22.text: Paul’s co-workers, including Tertius, send greetings

ROM.16.23-23.text: Gaius, Erastus, and Quartus send greetings

ROM.16.25-26.text: Paul praises God who strengthens believers by the gospel

ROM.16.27-27.text: Paul gives glory to the only wise God
